```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```
GTDB-Tk was used to classify the 14 selected metagenome bins by comparing their genome sequences with the Genome Taxonomy Database. The selected bins were copied into the GTDB-Tk genomes folder, and the classification analysis was conducted through SLURM. The SLURM classifications were examined to identify potential microbial groups associated with black band disease.

## Step 6: Taxonomic Classification with GTDB-Tk
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/gtdbtk

# Check genome folder
ls -ld genomes

# Display selected bin IDs
while read bin; do echo "$bin"; done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt

# Check paths to selected genome files
while read bin; do echo "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa"; done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt

# Copy selected bins into the GTDB-Tk genomes folder
while read bin; do cp "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa" genomes/; done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt

# Copy contig_328 separately because it was stored in the CheckM folder
cp ../checkm/bins_bbd/contig_328.fa genomes/

# Confirm all 14 genome files are present
ls genomes
ls genomes/*.fa | wc -l
```

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# Submit GTDB-Tk classification through SLURM
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/gtdbtk
sbatch run_gtdbtk.sh

# Check job status
squeue -u $USER
```

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# Check GTDB-Tk job completion
sacct -j 616 --format=JobID,State,ExitCode

# Examine taxonomic classification results
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/gtdbtk
ls -lh out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv
head -n 5 out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv
```

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# Save GTDB-Tk classification results
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/gtdbtk
cp out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv .
```

The taxonomic results varied across the 14 selected bins. Some bins could be assigned to bacterial groups - including the family Desulfovibrionaceae - and others remain unclassified.These results give insight about the microbial community associated with black band disease, but not all bins could be identified with certainty.
